cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Let Them Think They Won
cards.instruction: Protect someone’s confidence by hiding how much you softened the challenge, changed the terms, or withheld an advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Congratulations on winning the cake contest, Mum.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your cake isn't on the judging table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. It stayed in the kitchen where I can admire it privately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You still beat seven cakes that had every intention of winning.

mechanism: A takes charge of celebrating B achievement and controls which questions may displace it, concealing A withheld advantage to protect B confidence.
confusable: D205 hides A unfair advantage to protect A win; D207 hides A concession to protect someone else belief in their win.
comparison: Chess loser redirects attention from unused queen to B finishing move; cake entrant keeps A withdrawal secondary to Mum beating real competitors.
seedUse: Read both cards and all four seeds. Preserve B agency in noticing the concession and A sincere protective intent, not sarcastic patronizing praise.
